analysis.is_complaint_reason: The customer expresses dissatisfaction with a £12 late payment fee on their credit card and asks for it to be removed, alleging a small financial loss. Under CH-1 this is a complaint, although the customer accepts the payment was a day late.
analysis.summary: [PERSON_1] was charged a £12 late payment fee on their credit card, card ending [CARD_DIGITS_1]. They paid by bank transfer on the 15th, one day after the 14th due date, and say they forgot. They report never missing a payment in 6 years and ask for the fee to be removed as a one-off. The handler notes this is the first late fee on record in 12 months and found no vulnerability indicators. Under FEE-5 the fee appears correctly charged. FEE-3 lets a handler consider a discretionary goodwill refund. The decision rests with the handler. The customer prefers an email reply.

timeline.event: Customer paid by bank transfer, one day late
£12 late payment fee charged to the credit card
Handler noted first late fee in 12 months, no vulnerability indicators, and email preference

analysis.severity_reason: The financial loss is £12, which is under £100, and there are no fraud, vulnerability, legal or systemic factors (CH-6 Low).

vulnerability.suggested_support: None indicated. Reply by email as the customer prefers.

analysis.routing_reason: None of the ESC-1 triggers apply, so the complaints handler can resolve this directly. It may also suit a Summary Resolution Communication under CH-3.

policy_citations.quote: A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction, oral or written, about the bank's products, services or staff
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The customer is dissatisfied with the fee and asks for it to be removed.

policy_citations.quote: *Low*: financial loss under £100 or a service issue with no loss.
A late payment fee on a credit card is correctly charged if the minimum payment was not received by the due date.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The customer admits paying one day after the due date, so the fee appears correctly charged and not a bank error.

policy_citations.quote: a complaints handler may refund up to two fees of the same type in any rolling 12-month period as a goodwill gesture
policy_citations.how_it_applies: This is the first late fee in 12 months, so a discretionary refund is within the handler's authority. The decision is for the handler.

policy_citations.quote: Complaints handlers resolve complaints themselves unless one of the following applies

evidence.quote: I got charged a £12 late payment fee on my credit card.
I paid by bank transfer on the 15th but the due date was the 14th, so yes I was a day late, I forgot.
Can you take it off as a one-off?
First late fee on record in 12 months.

handover.complaint_summary: The customer was charged a £12 credit card late payment fee after paying one day late. They ask for a one-off removal, citing 6 years without a missed payment.
handover.desired_outcome: "Can you take it off as a one-off?"
actions_taken: Handler checked fee history: first late fee on record in 12 months (2026-11-03)
handover.vulnerability_assessment: The handler recorded no vulnerability indicators. The case does not record whether the customer was asked about support needs.
open_questions: Which month were the due date (14th) and payment (15th) in, and what was the date the fee was charged?

other_gaps: The month of the due date and payment is not stated.
There is no record that the customer was asked about support needs.
analysis.suggested_next_step: The handler should decide whether to apply a FEE-3 discretionary goodwill refund. The customer should then be replied to by email, and the complaint closed under CH-3 if it is resolved within 3 business days.
